extracted.intended_audience: prospective registered CTE apprenticeship program sponsors, Registration Agencies, State CTE Agencies, intermediaries, participating employers, and other stakeholders implementing or registering CTE apprenticeship programs
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and proposed requirements for developing, submitting, and operating registered Career and Technical Education (CTE) apprenticeship program standards, including sponsor responsibilities, program elements, registration submissions, and protections for apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: 900-hour minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the existing program design and outcomes provide evidence that the number of 900 hours should be lessened or whether the 900-hour floor is sufficient to train apprentices on core industry competencies in a work setting or if a higher number should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department requests comments addressing evidence from existing programs about the appropriateness of the 900-hour floor for CTE apprentices and whether adjustments are warranted for competency attainment or program design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive wage schedule and wage floor
rubrics_metrics.description: Program written standards must include wages the CTE apprentice will receive and a graduated schedule of progressively increasing wages during the apprenticeship term; entry wage may not be less than the FLSA minimum wage unless higher law or CBA requires otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The graduated wage schedule should increase over the apprenticeship term to reflect progressive acquisition of skills and competencies. The Department seeks comments on feasibility across industries and balancing continuous progressive wages with flexibility for industry needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination in wages and employee classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Wages paid by a sponsor or participating employer to a CTE apprentice must not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age (40 or older), genetic information, or disability; CTE apprentices who meet employee definitions must not be misclassified as independent contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reminder that part 30 requirements apply; sponsors and employers must ensure nondiscriminatory pay practices and proper classification consistent with tax and labor laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice-to-journeyworker ratio (safety-centered, Registration Agency approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must set an apprentice-to-journeyworker ratio that is approved by a Registration Agency and is consistent with proper safety, health, supervision, and training of the CTE apprentice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratio determination should center apprentice safety and consider factors that could endanger welfare (hazard exposure, risk of serious injury or death). While 1:1 has been common, sponsors may set different ratios based on industry, collective bargaining agreements, applicable laws, or blended training models; ratios must be specific and clearly described for particular work contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period limit (max 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered CTE apprenticeship program standards must include a probationary period that may not exceed 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter probation aligns with customary school course change periods and recognizes shorter OJT hours for CTE apprentices. Department requests comment on appropriateness for students and sponsors' operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation of adequate, safe, and accessible facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include an attestation that the sponsor will provide adequate, safe, and accessible facilities for training and supervision of apprentices, including accessibility for individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must comply with all applicable Federal, State, and local laws, including disability, occupational safety, and occupational health laws; the attestation is intended to ensure career pathways are available to everyone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for industry-recognized, hazard-tailored safety training
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include an attestation that the sponsor will provide adequate, industry-recognized safety training for apprentices in both on-the-job training and related instruction components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety training must be tailored to mitigate potential workplace hazards encountered in the covered industry skills framework OJT outline to ensure apprentice safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum qualifications for program entry (inclusive and achievable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must identify any minimum qualifications required by the sponsor and participating employers for entry into the CTE apprenticeship program, ensuring eligibility and paid OJT opportunities are inclusive, achievable, and standardized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges sponsors/employers may require prerequisites (e.g., coursework completion, attendance history). Department requests comment on whether sponsors/employers should be permitted to set minimum GPA requirements to obtain or maintain entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection procedures must comply with part 30 / Uniform Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Program standards must describe the program's method for selection of apprentices, and selection procedures must conform to 29 CFR 30.10 and the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (41 CFR part 60-3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection methods may be any combination so long as they evaluate adverse impact on race, sex, and ethnic groups and demonstrate business necessity where adverse impact exists; procedures must be applied uniformly, comply with Title I of the ADA and 29 CFR part 1630, and be facially neutral regarding protected characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive services disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors must provide a list of any supportive services that may be available to the CTE apprentice (e.g., childcare, transportation, equipment, tools, or other services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing supports provides apprentices awareness of available assistance arranged by sponsors or partner organizations and may coordinate with the workforce development system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced standing, credit, and increased wage process
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must grant advanced standing, credit, and increased wage when appropriate and include a process to reduce the usual term of OJT or related instruction based on prior qualifications or demonstrated expedited progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process must (i) be fair, transparent, and objective in identifying, assessing, and documenting prior learning or accelerated progress; and (ii) result in advanced standing, credit, and wage increases commensurate with progression granted. The proposal balances recognition of prior learning with minimum OJT hour requirements to prevent premature graduation without requisite proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against abbreviated OJT without justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The model requires minimum OJT hours while allowing advanced standing so that an apprentice does not have an abbreviated on-the-job training experience unless circumstances warrant it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures programs do not graduate apprentices before they have completed training and demonstrated requisite proficiency; acknowledges need for some OJT even after academic terms end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation of trainer and instructor qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Program standards must include an attestation documenting in writing that qualifications and experience of trainers and instructors providing OJT and related instruction satisfy the requirements in proposed §29.12 of subpart A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This acknowledgment allows the Registration Agency to ensure trainers are qualified and provides apprentices assurance they are trained by qualified individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Registration Agency and State CTE Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered CTE apprenticeship program sponsors must identify the Registration Agency and the State CTE Agency for which the program is being registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure coordinating entities are accurately identified and information is available to apprentices, parents/guardians, and Registration Agencies for reviews and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity pledge and conformity with part 30
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include the equal opportunity pledge as required in §30.3(c) and a statement that the program will be conducted, operated, and administered in conformity with all applicable provisions of 29 CFR part 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms program-level commitment to EEO requirements and provides regulatory basis for selection and administration practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint contact and complaint process information
rubrics_metrics.description: Program standards must include contact information for the appropriate party to address complaints within the program and information on how to file complaints with a Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures apprentices have avenues for raising issues internally and with the Registration Agency, and that apprentice agreements include complaint process information as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible program sponsors (types of organizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities eligible to be a sponsor include LEAs, institutions of higher education, State CTE Agencies, or another State government agency sharing responsibility for CTE; these entities may designate intermediaries by agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Perkins-eligible recipients and agencies have institutional experience administering CTE programs and can ensure rigorous academic standards and coordination of apprenticeship-related instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediary designation and expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A State CTE Agency, SEA, LEA, or institution may designate an intermediary to act as a program sponsor; intermediaries should have expertise in organizing and coordinating registered CTE apprenticeship programs or registered apprenticeship programs under subpart A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of qualifying intermediaries include joint apprenticeship and training committees, employers, trade associations, workforce boards, institutions of higher education, LEAs, and nonprofit entities experienced with Perkins funding. The Department seeks comment on feasibility and capacity of potential sponsors and intermediaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediary coordination and FERPA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated intermediaries must comply with subpart requirements and coordinate with Perkins educational institutions and agencies; they may need to share information in compliance with FERPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermediaries must coordinate to ensure sponsor requirements are met and should identify potential challenges and supports Registration Agencies and State CTE Agencies might provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission of registration (Standards Builder encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department anticipates requiring electronic submission of program registration applications and encourages use of the Standards Builder web-based platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submissions are expected to improve customer service, enable timely technical assistance, yield more responsive approvals, and allow OA to focus on technical assistance rather than non-electronic review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components for program registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A program sponsor must submit: (1) an OJT outline aligned with an industry skills framework; (2) a registered CTE apprenticeship-related instruction outline; (3) standards of registered CTE apprenticeship for the proposed program; and (4) the CTE apprenticeship agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These components capture core elements of a registered CTE apprenticeship program and ensure sponsors address training, instruction, standards, and agreements in submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan component: demonstrate diverse and inclusive participant selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must include a description of how students selected to participate reflect a diverse and inclusive cross-section of the current student body enrollment of participating secondary or postsecondary schools, consistent with 29 CFR part 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: demonstrate equitable opportunities for all students within the educational institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan component: alignment with existing CTE program
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must describe how the approved industry skills framework aligns with the existing CTE program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: ensure alignment between industrywide skills/competencies in an Administrator-approved industry skills framework and a State-approved CTE program; standards do not control local Perkins programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan component: recognized postsecondary credentials and pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must describe recognized postsecondary credentials the program may provide, how the program confers them, and their usefulness for entry into employment, registered apprenticeship under subpart A, postsecondary education, or combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: demonstrate likelihood the registered CTE apprenticeship provides educational credentials and pathways for apprentices' next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan component: employer safe and inclusive workplace assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must describe how they will ensure each participating employer has a record of maintaining a safe and inclusive workplace free from discrimination, violence, harassment, intimidation, and retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: protect safety and welfare of apprentices during OJT component and provide written assurance of employer workplace standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan component: access to career services and supportive services
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must describe how apprentices will have access to a broad range of career services and supportive services that enable participation in and successful completion of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: provide transparency to potential participants and families about supports available to overcome socioeconomic barriers to participation and completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan component: routine monitoring and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must describe how they will conduct routine monitoring and oversight of all aspects of the registered CTE apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: ensure sponsors are aware of responsibilities to provide timely and accurate monitoring, allow Registration Agencies to take corrective action where necessary, and maintain program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan component: affirmative steps to adhere to part 30
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must include a written description of how the program will take affirmative steps to adhere to the requirements of 29 CFR part 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors proposed §29.10(a)(8) concepts and is updated to account for registered CTE apprenticeship programs and apprentices; purpose is to show proactive compliance with EEO requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances that participating parties agree and formalize commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must provide a written assurance that parties involved in program operation (employers, partnering educational institutions, intermediaries) agree to specific commitments, roles, and responsibilities addressed in program standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurance must state that such agreements will be formalized through memoranda of understanding or other written agreements to demonstrate stakeholder engagement and allow Registration Agencies to hold sponsors accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records maintenance and retention assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must provide a written assurance that, consistent with §29.18, they will maintain any records the Registration Agency considers necessary to determine compliance with this part and applicable laws; records will be subject to a records retention requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: provide Registration Agencies access to pertinent records for program reviews and compliance activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional responsibilities for intermediaries designated as sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermediaries designated as program sponsors must comply with subpart requirements, coordinate with Perkins educational institutions and agencies, electronically submit written assurances, and comply with State/local laws and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department recognizes intermediaries may need to coordinate sharing information in compliance with FERPA and requests input on challenges and opportunities for intermediaries to meet sponsor requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor standards adoption agreement for participating employers
rubrics_metrics.description: A written sponsor standards adoption agreement is required between a sponsor and a participating employer (reached outside collective bargaining) obligating participating employers to comply with the sponsor's standards and the requirements of 29 CFR parts 29 and 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because employers are not eligible sponsors in this model, requiring an adoption agreement ensures employers adhere to standards, bolstering program accountability and protecting apprentice safety and welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement content and purpose (terms and education)
rubrics_metrics.description: All registered CTE apprenticeship programs must develop an apprenticeship agreement containing the terms and conditions of the training and instruction plan, including program's terms and conditions for education of registered CTE apprentices, in addition to employment and training terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The apprenticeship agreement is a foundational tool that clarifies terms, protects apprentice welfare, serves as a verifiable record, communicates benefits and intended outcomes, and promotes transparency and accountability among parties.
